-97.75140,30.34720.name: Texas Fertility Center, Vaughn, Silverberg & Associates
-97.75140,30.34720.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Kaylen Silverberg, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

0.67387,40.77354.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Noveprim Europe Ltd.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.65638,52.81779.name: Burton Fertility Clinic
-1.65638,52.81779.state: Burton Fertility Clinic, Queen’s Hospital, Belvedere Rd, Burton-on-Trent, DE13 0RB
-1.65638,52.81779.company: Satellite clinic to TFP Nurture Fertility
-1.65638,52.81779.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to TFP Nurture Fertility. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-0.08800,51.51800.name: Genomics England
-0.08800,51.51800.desc: The national programme that sequenced 100,000 genomes and now holds one of the largest linked genomic and health datasets in the world, publicly owned. Access is granted to researchers including commercial ones under controlled terms, so the arrangement is a working test of whether a public genomic asset can be used by industry without being handed to it.

-0.08800,51.51800.name: Syncona
-0.08800,51.51800.desc: A UK investment company that builds cell and gene therapy businesses rather than buying into them, founded with Wellcome Trust money. Company creation on this model means a single investor chooses which scientific programmes become companies at all, which is a narrower gate than a competitive funding round.

10.75220,59.91390.name: Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global — ethics exclusions
10.75220,59.91390.desc: The world's largest sovereign wealth fund, with an ethics council that can exclude companies from the portfolio and publishes its reasons for doing so. Divestment by an investor this size is one of the few sanctions that reaches a company without a regulator or a court, and the published reasoning becomes a reference other investors cite.

7.44740,46.94800.name: Swiss GMO moratorium — Federal Office for the Environment
7.44740,46.94800.desc: Switzerland has extended its moratorium on growing engineered crops repeatedly since 2005, most recently to 2027, while continuing to import engineered feed and to host some of the largest agricultural biotechnology companies in the world. A country can prohibit the cultivation and house the industry at once, and this is the clearest case of it.

-1.53470,12.35690.name: Agence Nationale de Biosécurité (Burkina Faso)
-1.53470,12.35690.desc: The national biosafety agency, which parliament converted from a departmental body into an administrative entity with its own legal authority and independent management. That change was made in the same period the country was withdrawing Bt cotton, and the sequence is the point: a regulator gains independence most readily just after the thing it was regulating has gone wrong. West Africa's biosafety decisions are made here and in Abuja more than anywhere else on the continent, and this agency is the one whose country has actually reversed a commercial approval.
